headline: OC Premium Small Companies Fund holds Megaport as a conviction position following AI infrastructure contracts and capital raise
reasoning: Megaport rebounded +208.2% during the quarter from three-year lows as investors reassessed its opportunity in AI infrastructure following the acquisition of Latitude.sh. The company announced four US-based AI infrastructure contracts with a combined total contract value of A$458.9m, focused on AI inference — where speed, reliability, and proximity to end users is critical, making MP1's global network footprint particularly relevant. To support these contracts, MP1 conducted a fully underwritten A$827m entitlement offer to fund GPU, network and storage hardware as well as a globally distributed on-demand GPU Pool. quote: Megaport (MP1, +208.2%) was the Fund's standout performer during the quarter, rebounding strongly from three-year lows in early April as investors reassessed the company's opportunity in AI infrastructure following the acquisition of Latitude.sh. The key development was MP1's announcement of four US-based AI infrastructure contracts with a combined total contract value of A$458.9m. These contracts are focussed on AI inference, which is the stage where trained AI models are used in real time by customers and applications. Unlike model training, inference is more sensitive to speed, reliability, and proximity to end users, which makes MP1's global network footprint particularly relevant. We view the strategy as a logical extension of MP1's existing network-as-a-service platform. By combining connectivity with access to distributed compute capacity across more than 1,100 data centres in 31 countries, MP1 is positioning itself to help customers deploy AI workloads closer to where they are needed. While execution risk remains given the scale of the capital raise and build-out, the announced contracts provide a stronger foundation for the company's AI infrastructure ambitions and support our positive view on the long-term demand outlook.

headline: Mission-critical ERP software with high switching costs and AI-driven module growth shields it from disruption

Counter-intuitively, Technology One is actually seeing an acceleration of growth driven by AI, as customers buy more modules to accelerate AI capability within their organisations. quote: On Technology One, we've added to our position in Technology One. Technology One is an ERP software provider focused on the education as well as local government segment. It's mission-critical software and has very high switching costs, so very difficult to rip out any ERP software in an organisation. We believe that the proprietary data that runs through the ERP platform, as well as the knowledge of the workflow and the sticky nature of the customer base, will mean it's very difficult to disrupt Technology One. Technology One themselves have actually seen an acceleration of growth in their business on the back of AI. They're finding that customers want to buy more modules of Technology One to accelerate their AI capability within their organisation. The other thing we like about the business is the strong management team. They've been able to navigate through many technological changes and pivoted the business through different revenue models, so we view that as a great buying opportunity on the back of the drawdown in technology stocks.
